title: Incolor SSR Review - A Chinese Aero Bike With Insane Specs!

takeaways.text: The test bike weighed 7.05 kg with cages and computer mount, without bottles or computer; it uses a 35.5 cm cockpit.
Repeats Incolor's claim of 4 W faster than a Cervélo S5 at 45 km/h, noting it comes from a ±20° yaw sweep where most of the gain is at wide angles; Cyclingnews had not yet tunnel-tested it.

Integrated seat mast cut to length, with swappable saddle clamps for limited height adjustment; maximum tire 32 mm with 2× or 36 mm with 1×. Tested on 28 mm GP5000s, then 32 mm tires on deeper wheels.

The reviewer called it the most uncomfortable bike he had ridden: harsh at the integrated seat mast and very stiff front end (tingling fingers after 45 minutes), skittish on rough British roads; 32 mm tires helped only slightly.
It feels fast and climbs like a light bike, matching the spec sheet, but the stiffness makes long rides unpleasant.
Frameset US$4,399 in August 2026, plus US$420 for the cockpit and US$600 for the taller-shorter or longer-lower custom geometry option.

disclosure: Cyclingnews tech review; the video segment is sponsored by a helmet brand unrelated to Incolor, and no Incolor commercial relationship is stated.
summary: Independent Cyclingnews road test of the Incolor SSR built as a complete bike; wind-tunnel results were promised for a later update.
